description: A real `docker pull paulgauthier/aider`, plus two near-miss tags an exact route must decline.
why: The only scenario that asserts an `image` identifier against a live registry, and the reason the catalog no longer carries a fixture-backed one. `deep: true` is what makes it possible: containers.sql is `expensive`, so it is absent from dist/discovery-linux.sql and this scenario asserts against `bin/discover --deep` instead -- the same artifact and the same bounded runner that ship. The controls are the half that makes it a test: `paulgauthier/aider-fork` has the catalogued value as a PREFIX, so declining it proves the route compares whole repository names and not substrings, and forbid_evidence is how that is asserted -- `correctly declined` and `never looked at` are the same shape without it.
known_gaps: A pull proves the registry still serves this repository under this name. It does not prove the image is the vendor's: an image name is chosen by whoever tags it, so `docker tag alpine paulgauthier/aider` produces the same finding. That is a property of container images and is recorded in the blind spots, not something a scenario can close.
Nothing here runs the image. `docker_containers` needs a per-container inspect document osquery reads strictly, so what a running container is doing stays out of scope.
